# jumpcloud_role (Resource)

Manages a JumpCloud administrative role.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Read-only auditor role scoped to the whole organization.
resource "jumpcloud_role" "auditor" {
  name        = "Security Auditor"
  description = "Read-only access for compliance reviews"

  permissions = [
    { resource_type = "users", action = "readonly" },
    { resource_type = "systems", action = "readonly" },
    { resource_type = "policies", action = "readonly" },
  ]

  scope = {
    type = "all"
  }
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) The name of the role.
- `permissions` (Attributes List) List of permission grants for this role. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--permissions))

### Optional

- `description` (String) Description of the role.
- `scope` (Attributes) Scope restriction for the role (all resources or a specific scope group). (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--scope))

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) The ID of the role.

<a id="nestedatt--permissions"></a>
### Nested Schema for `permissions`

Required:

- `action` (String) The action allowed on the resource type.
- `resource_type` (String) The resource type this permission applies to.


<a id="nestedatt--scope"></a>
### Nested Schema for `scope`

Required:

- `type` (String) Scope type: all or scope_group.

Optional:

- `id` (String) The scope group ID (required when type is scope_group).

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
terraform import jumpcloud_role.example <role-id>
```
